application_guidance.input_pattern: A maximal-monotone inclusion with an available approximate-resolvent sequence and summable certified absolute errors.
read_original_when: Reusing the boundedness-to-existence ball reduction requires checking the cited external maximality and existence results.
Seeking finite accuracy bounds, a convergence rate, relative-error variants or a different Oracle realization.
sensitive_conditions: Use boundedness or existence of a zero; without either, convergence is not concluded.
A positive uniform lower bound on c_k is required.
Errors tending merely to zero do not replace summability.
Weak convergence in a general Hilbert space is not a strong-convergence claim.

complexity_scope.guarantee: Deterministic asymptotic weak convergence, conditional on boundedness or zero existence, with the boundedness equivalence stated separately.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: No finite iteration bound or accuracy-dependent complexity constant is supplied by this Theorem.
complexity_scope.oracle: An approximate resolvent satisfying the absolute error condition; no primitive-gradient, value or graph-evaluation Oracle realization is assumed free.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: The whole iterate sequence converges weakly to a zero; ||Q_k(z^k)|| and ||z^(k+1)-z^k|| tend to zero in norm. This is not a finite-output accuracy certificate.
complexity_scope.regime: An infinite sequence; summable absolute errors; inf_k c_k>0; real Hilbert space.
complexity_scope.resource: One abstract approximate-resolvent request per outer iteration in the selected interface; inner-solve and certification costs are unspecified.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Sequences generated by the specified proximal point iteration under criterion (A), including (A') as a sufficient implementation criterion.

map: Printed p.883, Eq.(2.6): if zbar is a zero, resolvent nonexpansiveness and criterion (A) give ||z^(k+1)-zbar|| <= ||z^k-zbar||+epsilon_k. Iteration and summability give boundedness.

Printed pp.883–884, Eqs.(2.7)–(2.10): for an arbitrary bounded generated sequence choose s>0 bounding ||z^k|| and exceeding every epsilon_k. Add the normal cone of the closed radius-2s ball, represented as the subdifferential of its indicator h, to form T'=T+partial h. Resolvent points lie inside that ball, so the same iteration is retained. The source invokes its external maximal-monotone sum theorem and Proposition 2 to obtain maximality and a zero for T'; near each weak cluster point T'=T. This is the source's reduction, not a local replacement argument.

Printed p.884, Eqs.(2.11)–(2.13): Proposition 1(c) at a zero supplies the complementary-residual inequality. Combining it with boundedness and the absolute error bound gives Eq.(2.12), while the summably perturbed distance recurrence makes ||z^k-zbar|| converge.

Printed p.884, Eq.(2.5) and Eq.(2.14): take limits in Eq.(2.12) to obtain ||Q_k(z^k)||->0. The update error then gives ||z^(k+1)-z^k||->0. The positive lower bound on c_k gives c_k^(-1)Q_k(z^k)->0 strongly.

Printed pp.884–885, Eq.(2.15): monotonicity against any graph point, weak convergence along a cluster subsequence and the strongly vanishing graph residual imply <z-z^infinity,w> >=0 for every w in T(z). Maximality identifies each weak cluster point as a zero. For the ball-modified operator this transfers back by agreement with T inside the ball.

Printed p.885, Eq.(2.16) and subsequent squared-distance expansion: distances to each possible weak cluster point have limits. Two different weak cluster points would force both mu_2^2-mu_1^2>0 and mu_1^2-mu_2^2>0. Hence the bounded sequence has a unique weak cluster point and converges weakly; this also proves necessity in the boundedness characterization.

assumptions: T is maximal monotone on H.
c_k>0 for every integer k>=0 and inf_k c_k>0.
epsilon_k>=0 for every k>=0 and sum_(k=0)^infinity epsilon_k<infinity.
The entire sequence satisfies criterion (A); it suffices instead to satisfy (A'), by Proposition 3.
statement.conclusion: The sequence {z^k} is bounded if and only if Z is nonempty. If it is bounded (equivalently, if Z is nonempty), there is a point z^infinity in Z such that z^k converges weakly to z^infinity, and lim_(k->infinity)||Q_k(z^k)||=0=lim_(k->infinity)||z^(k+1)-z^k||. The limiting zero is particular to the sequence and is not asserted to be the only zero of T.
statement.objects_and_definitions: H is a real Hilbert space and T:H -> 2^H is maximal monotone. P_k=(I+c_k T)^(-1), Q_k=I-P_k, Z={z in H:0 in T(z)}. Criterion (A) means ||z^(k+1)-P_k(z^k)|| <= epsilon_k. S_k(z)=T(z)+c_k^(-1)(z-z^k); criterion (A') means dist(0,S_k(z^(k+1))) <= epsilon_k/c_k.
statement.parameter_domains: k ranges over the nonnegative integers; c_k are finite positive reals with a positive uniform lower bound; no upper bound or monotonicity assumption on c_k is imposed in Theorem 1; H may be infinite-dimensional.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such H,T, every starting point z^0 in H, every parameter and error sequence satisfying the assumptions, and every resulting iterate sequence obeying the error criterion. Deterministic statement with no stochastic guarantee.

summary: For summable absolute resolvent errors and positive parameters bounded away from zero, boundedness is equivalent to existence of a zero; in that case the iterates converge weakly to a zero and both displayed residual norms vanish.
title: Weak convergence of proximal point iteration under criterion (A)
use_when: Establish asymptotic convergence of a specified inexact proximal point sequence after verifying summable absolute errors and a positive lower parameter bound.
